reviewBasis: Checked against the active clue records in the event database and the GM staging instructions in story/. Photographs and printed evidence are produced by Print Studio; pictures of people are placeholders until you add your own (docs/evidence-photos.md).
statusNote: Preparation checklist only: nothing on it is bought, made or checked for you. Printed evidence and stationery are generated in Print Studio; the physical props, the decanter and the envelopes are yours to gather.

items.title: Distinctive private decanter with removable stopper
items.detail: Set on a small private drinks table or tray, visibly separate from general champagne service. The stopper matters to several witness accounts. Agree the location with Vincent, Dakota and Veronica (she must be able to reach it unseen).

items.title: Red wine or a suitable red grape-juice substitute
items.quantity: Enough for the rehearsed pour and toast
items.detail: Use an ordinary drink agreed with the performer in the private decanter. The decanter and the red wine are real and Vale drinks from them during the toast. Serve the guests champagne, so that Vale is visibly the only person drinking red: that is what puts Lucien's Round 1 observation in front of the whole room rather than leaving it on a card. Nothing is added to the real drink.

items.title: Vincent’s own drinking glass
items.detail: Keep it with the private decanter and rehearse where it is put down for the staged collapse. Keep general champagne glassware separate from the decanter and its glass.

items.title: Private drinks table or tray
items.detail: A practical surface for the decanter and glass, with an agreed spot beside it for Dakota’s compact-recovery account. This is staging support for the named objects.

items.title: Music player, speakers, power and audio leads
items.detail: Prepare Died in Your Arms Tonight; It Had To Be You (Dark Version); Lux Aeterna; Killer Queen; Summer of ’69 or the agreed dance set. Use the retained cue cards. Comeback Girl never plays.

items.title: Stage/disco lighting and an operator’s cue
items.detail: Rehearse the single twenty-second music-and-stage-light cue. Spinny leads: when his music rises Leo switches off some of the stage lights. House lights remain on. Check which stage lights Leo can switch off, who operates the controls and who gives the GM signal.

items.title: Working microphone and any spare batteries
items.detail: Useful for the welcome, toast and conclusion. The earlier broken microphone and two-second crackle are supplied recollections; no live fault or second distraction needs to be staged.

items.title: Clock or timer and discreet cue sheet
items.detail: Time the actual twenty-second cue. Fictional 19:29, 19:30 and 19:55 do not require the venue clock to show those times. No special visible evidence clock needs constructing.

items.title: Vincent-to-Peter change and private holding space
items.when: Ready before arrival; change in Round 1
items.detail: Keep Peter’s badge out of the arrival pack. Agree a discreet exit, change and re-entry. The taxi note accompanies Peter; no real twenty-five-minute wait is needed.

items.title: Empty silver compact marked VV and removable seal
items.quantity: 1 compact, with a simple removable seal
items.owner: GM → Scooter → Veronica → private drinks table → GM → Dakota → Scooter
items.detail: Deliver closed at arrival: Scooter hands it to Veronica in secret. During the toast music Veronica sets it unseen on the private drinks table beside the decanter. After the collapse the GM takes it from the table, removes the seal and gives it to Dakota. In Round 2 Scooter asks Dakota about it and borrows it to show Beverly. Keep it empty; C1 residue and the tests exist in the story/report.

items.title: Two matching deep-red envelopes
items.when: Spinny at arrival; Dakota in Round 2
items.detail: Use matching stock and matching typing. Leave senders anonymous. The Round 2 issue represents Dakota’s earlier fictional receipt; both guests retain their envelopes for Round 3 comparison.

items.title: Dummy payments for both envelopes
items.detail: Put a dummy payment in each deep-red envelope. Print the prop money from Print Studio (Evidence, "Prop money: Vale Meridian Glamour Pounds"): 24 notes, six to a landscape A4 sheet, cut along the marks and put 12 in each envelope. No real cash is needed.

items.title: Printed music and silence slips
items.detail: Music: “At the toast cue, raise the music for twenty seconds. No delays.” Silence: “Say nothing about what you saw near the drinks.” Keep each inside its corresponding envelope.

items.title: Taxi-driver journey note
items.detail: Passenger Peter Vale; collection outside the solicitor’s office, Cheltenham, 19:30; gala arrival 19:55; fictional date 10 October 1986. It supports the journey only, not the appointment or contract.

items.title: Laboratory report, one per table
items.quantity: 8 copies of CLUE_VV_R2, one per table, in Donna's Round 3 envelope (Item F)
items.detail: Print the report eight times (Print Studio, Evidence) and put all eight in Donna's Round 3 envelope. Her card tells her to hand one to every table at the start of the round, so everybody can read the same findings. It includes the compact/wine connection, different dish sedative and limited fabric finding. No actual sample packets are required.

items.title: Prepared decanter photograph
items.quantity: Part of Vance’s Round 2 pack, 9 copies
items.detail: Produced: print photo-decanter from Print Studio (Evidence). A woman from behind, her hand on the stopper, with the date and 19:29:10 in the caption; no powder transfer and no face. Black and white. The figure's recognisable features are long blonde hair, a dark draped gown with a pearl shoulder line, a wide cuff bracelet; keep them consistent with the murderer's costume, which should include a wide cuff bracelet on the right wrist.

items.title: Passport in Tina’s former identity
items.when: Hand to Nikki with her Round 2 clue (CLUE009)
items.detail: Prepare a printed theatrical old passport with Tina’s character photograph and the name Patricia Margaret Thatcher. Pack it with Nikki Neon’s Round 2 clue (CLUE009) and hand both to her at the start of Round 2. Nikki shows it to Tina and asks her to explain the name. The discovery under the sofa cushion is supplied in the clue; no planted document or search under venue cushions is needed.

items.title: Vance’s Polaroid camera
items.detail: His arrival card says he circulates with a Polaroid. A non-working period camera is enough for the role. Film is optional for party snapshots; the Round 3 evidence image is prepared separately or described.

items.title: Sabrina’s notebook and pen
items.detail: Her arrival card explicitly says Vale told her to bring a notebook. Useful character dressing as well as somewhere to make personal notes.

items.title: Polly’s claim folder
items.quantity: 1 folder or clipboard with a few blank claim forms
items.detail: A retired insurance assessor's prop, for the look only. Use blank forms; nothing in it is evidence. Her cards give everything she knows.

items.title: Beverly’s medical-style bag
items.detail: Her Round 1 card mentions her medical bag. An empty bag supports the character; drugs, medical equipment and real sample containers are unnecessary.

items.title: Ronnie Reels’ camera or camcorder
items.detail: Supports his filming role and east-wall camera position. No recording of a real poisoning or reconstructing the fictional sightline is required.

items.title: Veronica’s recognisable gown or evening outfit
items.detail: The gown is named in sightings and the fabric account. Use the guest’s chosen outfit; the pale hem trace and F1 swab are described on cards and the report. No real powder, marking or swabbing of clothing is required.

items.title: Coats, wrap and Vance’s photograph packs
items.detail: Print all nine photographs from Print Studio (Evidence) nine times and make up nine identical packs, one per table and one for Vance: greetings, a dance, a group conversation, champagne service, the lobby signing marked 7:28 pm, Lucien beside the mirror marked 7:05 pm, two further reception views, and the decanter frame. Hand them out at the start of Round 2, not before. A plain envelope for each pack keeps the dropped-prints moment with Nikki usable. The coats and wrap still support the pocket and cloakroom accounts; no live pocket insertion or search under cushions is needed.

items.title: Wellness/cosmetics display bottle
items.detail: A cosmetic accessory for the described product business. Keep it empty and separate from evidence; the cards supply ingredient and supplier information.

items.title: Penny’s notebook and pencil
items.quantity: 1 small notebook and pencil, if desired
items.detail: An ordinary notebook and pencil can suggest Penny’s script-editing work. No prepared speech, script pages, hidden writing or additional evidence needs to be made.

items.title: Clue and private performer/GM cards
items.detail: 51 arrival cards, then 52 in each of Rounds 1–3. Keep the toast and closing instructions private until their cues. The laboratory report is counted separately above.

items.title: Name badges, holders and seating stationery
items.quantity: 55 badges; 54 holders; 54 place cards; 8 table signs
items.detail: Badges are 90 × 56 mm with crop marks, eight per A4 sheet. One performer swaps Vincent for Peter, so two badges are printed for that seat but 54 holders suffice; Peter’s badge prints on its own private sheet. Use holders or clips that fit the finished badge size. Counts come from the approved seating plan.

items.title: Clue envelopes and their labels
items.quantity: 207 envelopes; 207 labels on 12 Avery J8161 sheets
items.detail: Every character gets their own envelope for each round: 51 in Round 0 and 52 in each of Rounds 1 to 3. Print the labels from Print Studio (Voting & notes) on Avery J8161 or L7161, 63.5 × 46.6 mm, eighteen per sheet. Each round starts a fresh sheet, so the sorting stays honest and the part-used sheet at the end of a round leaves spare labels for anything written by hand. Each label carries the guest name to read across a table, the character underneath to confirm the right card, and the table number. Envelopes need to take a 186 × 130 mm card, so C5 or a similar size.

items.title: Voting slips and pens
items.quantity: 56 slips; about 1 pen per attendee plus spares
items.detail: Tables use the slips while they discuss who committed the murder: one accused name, with the motive, means and opportunity. Nobody collects them. Pen quantities are a practical host suggestion.

items.title: Private note sheets and spare plain paper
items.detail: The print app supplies To, From and a lined Message area, two A5 notes per landscape A4 sheet. Writing a note remains optional; guests can speak directly.

items.title: GM references, round dividers and packing supplies
items.quantity: The GM reference sheets; 8 release dividers; labelled folders/envelopes
items.detail: Keep the running order, this checklist, the envelope inclusions list and the guest lookup to hand. Use scissors or a trimmer, cream A4 paper/card and spare seals for preparation. Packing envelopes are distinct from the two deep-red evidence envelopes.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Covered dish, disturbed seal and service label
items.detail: The dish has already been withdrawn in the supplied account. No separate food exhibit, cooked special dish or real sedative is needed. D1 is represented in the laboratory report.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Broken guitar, smashed champagne glass and broken microphone
items.detail: These are earlier incidents at about 19:20–19:21. Do not break real items to recreate them. Optional dummy costume instruments add atmosphere only.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Ignition cable, guardrail and rehearsal inspection
items.detail: The isolated cable, stage positions and old inspection form establish accounts. No pyrotechnics, working ignition device, extra barrier or forged inspection sheet needs preparing.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Recordings, tapes, archive computer and Comeback Girl
items.detail: No working archive, CG-1 audio, transcripts or performance film needs making. Comeback Girl is never played. Ordinary party music remains required above.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Contracts, financial records and other paperwork
items.detail: No contract bundle, will, loan papers, supplier records, conviction file, guest-list leak, publicity note, poem or signature specimen is required. Guests use their supplied knowledge; the taxi note and lab report are the specific printed documents listed above.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Chemical samples, medicines, fabric swab and herbs
items.detail: The compact stays empty. No stimulant, sedative, costume powder, C1/W1/D1/F1 sample pots or real testing is needed.

items.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
items.title: Handcuffs, restraint and an epilogue jacket note
items.detail: The arrest is a spoken invitation to accompany Donna, with no restraint required. The retained epilogue explicitly needs no extra prop.
